comments.author: Miserable_Ad2837
comments.body:
dont use google earth, use the actual map data, its free and its vectors not photos. thats what makes the stylized part easy, you get roads, buildings, forests, rivers, field shapes as polygons and draw them however you want.  
openstreetmap has all of that for the whole planet. elevation: copernicus dem is 30m global, most european countries give lidar for free, 1m or better. land cover: esa worldcover, 10m, tells you whats forest, crop, grass, water everywhere on earth.  
no ai needed for this part. download the data as shapefiles or geojson, open in qgis to see what you have, then a python script with geopandas and shapely cuts out your area and writes json: roads with widths, field polygons, forests, water, building footprints. elevation comes as geotiff, rasterio reads it into a heightmap. in the engine you read the json and place stuff: terrain from the heightmap, roads as meshes along the lines, trees scattered inside forest polygons, buildings on footprints. same input, same world every time.  
im doing this for a farming game, 1024 hectares of real countryside from the national map data, real roads and real field shapes. the data part took a few weaks. the hard part is that real terrain is boring in most places and you still have to make it look good. planet size i wouldnt, pick a region and do it properly
